correctness.rationale: For every labeling, the first A-class with a zero and last B-class with a zero form a unique frontier pair. Nested neighborhoods and nonnegative labels make every zero on each side defensible iff the one critical opposite-side prefix/suffix has weight >=2. The W=U-V factor enforces presence of a zero in the frontier class; V enforces positive labels outside the frontier; truncation T_2 deletes exactly weight-0 and weight-1 failures. Thus the cell polynomials multiply and partition all valid functions, proving the p(p+1)-term identity for all positive class sizes. Boundary frontiers p+1 and 0 are handled without truncation. Independent brute force checked 793620 actual vertex labelings, 76 profiles and all 1143 frontier cells from the current verify.py file; finite tests do not establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The motivating recent work explicitly studies all-weight Italian domination, while previous chain-graph results give minimum values only. The new theorem is a complete natural-family weight distribution for arbitrary Ferrers/twin-class profiles, expressed by an explicit p(p+1) frontier decomposition and factored polynomial products rather than exponential enumeration. It distinguishes graphs with the same bipartition cardinalities and identical minimum Italian weight (six-vertex examples yield 4 versus 6 weight-four functions), giving genuine information beyond the prior optimum. This is an infinite-class exact enumerator with plausible use for counting feasible defense placements, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice or a formal substitution.
